headline: Brazil's Bovespa crashed 13.9 percent on Lula's re-election while Anthropic's IPO filing lifted Wall Street tech
subhead: The S&P 500 rose 0.7 percent and Brent fell 5.8 percent to 109.97 dollars before Wednesday's Fed decision; US single-stock and most Indian prices in this feed still show Friday's close because Monday's data had not posted.

us.text: The S&P 500 rose 0.7 percent to 7,676.8 and the Nasdaq 0.8 percent Monday as oil eased and Anthropic's IPO filing lifted tech.
Meta launched a plan to raise up to 95 billion dollars in stock, about 35 billion upfront, to fund its AI build-out.
The Fed decides Wednesday with a hold at 3.75 to 4.00 percent the consensus; the 10-year yield sits at 4.99 percent.

india.text: The Nifty rose 153.2 points to 22,753.2 and the Sensex 482.9 points Monday on metal and pharma buying, ending a four-day slide.
Provisional data showed FIIs net sold 1,462 crore rupees of cash equities Monday while DIIs net bought 2,610 crore rupees.
The rupee fell 22 paise to 95.15 per dollar, a third straight loss, as elevated crude and foreign selling weighed.

global.text: Brazil's Bovespa plunged 13.9 percent to 176,608 and the real sank after Lula's surprise re-election, forcing a trading halt.
The STOXX 600 rose 0.77 percent to 640.66 Monday as easing oil and upbeat corporate updates lifted shares.
Korea's Kospi is up 2.8 percent early Tuesday, led by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, as Anthropic's IPO push lifted chip stocks.

weekly.narrative: Two forces ran the week and both pointed at the cost of capital. Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, including Iranian claims that seven vessels were hit or mined, took Brent above 117 dollars and WTI past 100, and because that lands as an inflation shock rather than a growth scare it lifted rate expectations instead of safe havens: gold closed the week below 4,000 dollars and now sits 1.7 percent above its 52 week low and silver hit a year to date low, while the US 10 year held near 4.99 percent. The second force was the AI financing question, which moved from equity multiples to credit, with a Lam Research warning on chip supply into 2027 knocking the Nasdaq 2.6 percent on Thursday, CoreWeave 2032 bonds quoted near 78 cents on the dollar, and Jensen Huang arguing the sector is short of capital rather than demand. India inverted the pattern, with the Nifty pressured by the oil bill and foreign selling while IT rallied on a reverse AI trade that reads weaker AI capex as work returning to traditional services firms, and the rupee closed at 94.93 against the dollar. Next week stacks the catalysts: the Fed decision on 28 October with a hike priced near 7.6 percent, Microsoft and Alphabet that same evening, Amazon plus Q3 GDP and September PCE on 29 October, the Bank of Japan on 30 October, and in Mumbai the listing of the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms issue alongside five new mainboard IPOs.
